fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can distinguish it from the surrounding area.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around all sides of it.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Post the location of any rear gate or secondary access point on or near the front of the property so arriving responders do not have to search for it.
• Keep any gate or fence opening along the perimeter unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.
• Clear a staging area near the access drive wide enough for a fire apparatus to park without blocking its own exit.
• Thin dense vegetation at the rear of the property to give responders a visible working area behind the structures.
• Keep the walkway and patio area free of stored items so responders can move between the front and rear of the main residence without detours.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the structure to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing beneath and between scattered trees near the structure.
• Keep the area directly around the structure clear of tall grass, weeds, and low-growing plants.
• Maintain open ground between the scattered trees and the structure by mowing or cutting ground vegetation regularly.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation under large trees where it has accumulated.
